chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, raising it, who said:
Regarding the prescribed punishment in travel, where if one commits adultery he is not stoned if he is muḥṣan, he said: “If he shortens the prayer and breaks the fast, then he is not muḥṣan.”

key_terms.أَفْطَرَ: broke the sawm (fast) due to travel
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, carrying legal consequences in fiqh
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: legally muḥṣan, i.e. possessing the qualifying marital status for this hadd ruling
key_terms.يُرْجَمْ: be stoned as a legal punishment

ai.seo_question: Does a traveler remain muḥṣan for the hadd ruling of zina if he shortens prayer and breaks his fast?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the status of iḥṣān during travel in relation to the hadd of zina. It indicates that a traveler who qualifies to shorten salat (prayer) and break the sawm (fast) is not treated as muḥṣan for the purpose of rajm.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5037 - Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya narrated from Muhammad bin Al-Husayn in a marfu' report, who said:

Regarding the prescribed punishment (hadd) in travel, in which if one commits adultery, he is not stoned if he is married, it was said:
"If he shortens the prayer and breaks his fast, then he is not considered married (muhsan)."
